newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican president rules out Indian segregation.
newsitem.headline: Mexican president rules out Indian segregation.

text.p: In comments aimed at Zapatista guerrillas, Mexican President Ernesto Zedillo on Thursday flatly ruled out the segregation of Indians in his country.

"We will not permit segregation in Mexico," Zedillo told a gathering of Nahuat, Tenek and Pame Indians in the central state of San Luis Potosi, the latest stop in a campaign blitz by Zedillo aimed at Indians.
Zedillo's government is trying to reach a peace agreement with the predominantly Maya Indian rebels of the Zapatista National Liberation Front in the southeastern state of Chiapas.

Talks broke off four months ago and suffered another setback this month when Zapatista leader Subcommander Marcos denounced the government's proposed constitutional amendments on Indian rights as "a cruel and insolent hoax for the struggle of Indian people in Mexico."
The government then condemned the Zapatistas as separatists who wanted to remove Mexico's nearly nine million Indians from the jurisdiction of the central government.
The Zapatistas remain in the Chiapas jungle, where they are surrounded by the Mexican army as a ceasefire holds.
Zedillo on Thursday rejected "special powers" that would only further isolate and marginalize Mexican Indians.
For their part, the Indians complained to Zedillo about how they continue to lag behind the remainder of Mexico.
"We have waited many years without being served by our government," Mateo Andrade told Zedillo, the first president in 63 years to visit Xilitla. "We've become used to being poor."
